title: Markov Random Fields & Factor Graphs
interviewAnswer: An MRF is an undirected graphical model whose joint distribution is expressed with local compatibility factors; it is useful when dependencies are symmetric rather than naturally directed.
why: MRFs underpin structured prediction and spatial/image models.
intuition: Neighboring pixels can prefer similar labels without one pixel causing the other.
deepDive: The joint density is proportional to a product of positive potentials and requires a partition function for normalization, which can make inference difficult.
commonMistakes: Reading causal direction from an undirected graph.
followUps: Why is the partition function hard?
production: Large MRFs often require approximate inference; validate both quality and latency.
workedExample: Image segmentation can combine per-pixel evidence with pairwise smoothness between neighbors.
